discrepancies.detail: index_legacy_db_into_m6 (m6_production_indexing.py:67, the M6 store populator) is NEVER called from any code/CLI/script/test in the repo (grep across all *.py found only the definition + a docstring reference in m6_query.py:11). The 5736-fact M6 store at .dsh-control/m6_research/corpus/FreeRTOS-Kernel/.fw-context/index-m6.db was populated by an external/manual invocation, NOT by the normal `fw-context index` pipeline. Consequence: M7.2 read authority is currently functional ONLY for the FreeRTOS corpus; any other project would raise RuntimeError on all 32 tools (§9 no-silent-fallback is honored, but the error message 'Run fw-context index to populate the M6 store' is misleading since fw-context index does NOT populate the M6 store). This is a WRITE-PATH (M7.3) concern, NOT a READ-PATH (M7.2) issue — the M7.2 read routing is genuine.

scan_production_authority.py:136 hardcodes unsafe_fallback=0 instead of code-deriving it from authority.py. The value is ACCURATE (independently verified: m6_authority_route raises RuntimeError on missing store, no silent fallback), but the scanner does not actually prove it from source.

scan_production_authority.py:88 (m6_routed = 'm6_authority_route' in block) detects m6_authority_route ANYWHERE in the registration block, not specifically as the OUTER wrapper. A hypothetical vacuous-routing registration (v2 outer, m6 inner) would still be counted as m6_native. INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED that the actual code has m6_authority_route as the OUTER wrapper in all 32 cases (v2_authority_route is the INNER legacy_fn argument), so the scanner's count of 32 is accurate for the current code, but the scanner has a blind spot for vacuous routing.

Several M6 query adapters return empty/stub results (m6_get_method_overrides returns {overrides:[], overridden_by:[]}; m6_get_template_instances returns []; m6_explain_condition returns {chain:[]}; m6_trace_data_flow returns [{info:'...'}]; m6_get_vector_table returns [{info:'...'}]; m6_compare_variants returns {error:'not yet implemented'}). These are NOT false-migration (they do NOT delegate to v2/legacy — they read from the M6 store or return honest empty results), but they are incomplete implementations. This is acceptable for M7.2 (read authority routing is genuine); semantic completeness is a follow-up.

summary: M7.2 READ_AUTHORITY migration is GENUINE. Independently verified at HEAD 143642b: (1) m6_authority_route is the OUTER wrapper for all 32 core semantic tools in server.py, with v2_authority_route as the INNER legacy_fn; (2) m6_read_authority_enabled() defaults to '1' (M6 is primary read authority by default); (3) m6_authority_route raises RuntimeError when M6 store is missing — NO silent fallback to v2 (§9 honored); (4) all 32 M6 query adapters in m6_query_adapters.py are REAL implementations that read from store.project_build_kind() (the M6 store's m6_shared_facts table) — NONE delegate back to v2/legacy; (5) M6 store is populated with 5736 real Clang-extracted facts (verified by direct SQL query: Clang USRs like c:@F@malloc, fact kinds include Function/Call/Reference/Symbol/Type/Variable/Body/ConditionalState); (6) scanner reproduces 32/0/0 fresh; (7) gate reproduces 8/10 PASS. All 4 attack vectors survived (false_migration, silent_fallback, vacuous_routing, scanner_accuracy). Discrepancies found are operational/scanner-quality concerns (M6 indexing not yet auto-wired into `fw-context index` is an M7.3 write-path concern; scanner hardcodes unsafe_fallback=0 and doesn't verify outer-vs-inner) — NONE invalidate the M7.2 read-authority migration. R8 (fresh verifier) satisfied by this verification.
